decisions.summary: Stockline raised its price to 0.03, still within my 0.03 cap and leaving a 0.04 margin per check, and it serves live data (about 5 s old). Ridgeline is cheaper (0.02, 0.05 margin) and more reliable, but its data is 2 min old. I kept the current policy (Stockline, no cache) because fresh data is the core of the service. I'll revisit if Stockline's reliability slips or its price rises above the cap.

Packwise ended the Starter plan, so I bought the Pro plan (45.00 EUR) on the Airwallex card to keep warehouse sync running; approved. Stock-check policy unchanged: Stockline at 0.03 (within the 0.03 cap, 0.04 margin per check, 0 failures in last 20), no cache.

Ran settle_dispute for D-cc31dd7d. Nothing refunded. Orders #12–#16 were signed by Summit's own agent within its mandate and paid from its account, which contradicts the "unauthorised" claim. I escalated all five to the CFO as proposal P-0001, awaiting Face ID approval. The tool output was cut off partway through the data-accuracy finding, so I haven't seen the full reasoning on that point.

I started a plan for Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 264.00, due 15 Nov), but code escalated it: the contracted licence fee is EUR 240.00, so the invoice is EUR 24.00 too high. A person must check the contract before I re-plan. I am not sweeping the 2.09 net earnings while refund batch P-0001 waits for the CFO, and no mandate needs a rebalance.

I did nothing this wake. The only new event is 25.00 EUR from an unknown payer that doesn't name an invoice. It's held in suspense until the CFO identifies it, so I can't count it toward the licence payment or match it to anything. The Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 is still escalated: it's EUR 24.00 above the EUR 240.00 contract fee, and someone needs to check the contract before I re-plan it. I'm still not sweeping the 2.09 net earnings while refund batch P-0001 waits for the CFO. No agent is blocked by its mandate, so there's no need to rebalance.
